debate_title: AI governance frameworks for advanced AI systems

conflicts.point: Whether pre-market registration thresholds and administrative safety cases prevent systemic risk or merely establish compliance barriers that entrench market monopolies.

positions.stance: Argues that pre-market registration at frontier scale provides necessary gatekeeping to verify safety controls before code executes at civilizational scale.
Argues that pre-market registration creates compliance moats that protect incumbent labs and stifle open-source innovation.

conflicts.point: Whether post-market liability and dynamic insurance pools can adequately handle catastrophic systemic failures where damages exceed corporate solvency.

positions.stance: Argues that post-market financial penalties and lawsuits fail when damages exceed corporate solvency and destruction occurs instantly across millions of devices.
Argues that dynamic risk-conditioned capital requirements and real-time telemetry-conditioned insurance pools absorb systemic variance better than brittle administrative paperwork.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-market registration thresholds and administrative safety cases prevent systemic risk or merely establish compliance barriers that entrench market monopolies.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist and skeptic arguments succeed because they identify structural flaws in static administrative oversight. Model weights change continuously, which renders point-in-time safety cases legally and technically brittle.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that dynamic compliance frameworks can update continuously without creating prohibitive administrative bottlenecks for smaller developers would overturn this verdict.

verdicts.conflict: Whether post-market liability and dynamic insurance pools can adequately handle catastrophic systemic failures where damages exceed corporate solvency.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions rely on theoretical projections regarding catastrophic tail risk and insurance capacity. Without empirical benchmarks for systemic algorithmic damages exceeding corporate balance sheets, neither mechanism can claim proven reliability.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Actuarial data from real-world deployments showing that telemetry-conditioned insurance pools can absorb correlated frontier AI failures would resolve the deadlock.
